items.title: 1 · Listen
items.body: Listen for proposals, concerns, evidence, and agreement. Middle-stage notes make closing easier: record a participant's name, main idea, reasoning, connections, and unresolved concerns.

items.title: 2 · Connect
items.body: Look for complementary ideas, a proposal that addresses another's weakness, concerns that suggest a shared solution, or recommendations that could form a coordinated strategy.

items.title: 3 · Credit
items.body: Identify whose contributions you use: “Building on Maya's suggestion and Jordan's concern…” Credit demonstrates listening. Never claim another participant's idea as your own.

items.title: 4 · Advance
items.body: Add something new: a combined proposal, resolved tension, implementation condition, priority, compromise, or next decision. Merely naming two speakers is not enough.
